e ultra fast casting method by which complex aluminium alloys are produced with cooling speeds of over 1 million ºC per second. During the production process molten aluminium is casted upon a rotating copper wheel. The liquid aluminium alloy solidifies in a fraction of a second in a thin, long ribbon, resulting in a material with a very fine and homogenous micro- or nanostructure. ed learning. Since 2000, HUG hosts the RAFT project, a distance education and telemedicine network aimed at supporting healthcare professionals in sub-saharan Africa. The RAFT was first developed in Mali, then in Mauritania, Morocco, Cameroon, Burkina-Faso, Senegal, Tunisia, Ivory Coast, Madagascar, Niger, Burundi, Congo-Brazzaville, Algeria, Chad, and Benin. In 2008, it started its expansion in English-speaking Africa. The core activity of the RAFT is the webcasting of interactive courses targeted to physicians and other care professionals, the topics being proposed by the partners of the network. Courses are webcast every week, freely available, and followed by hundreds of professionals who can interact directly with the presenter(s). 70% of these courses are now produced and webcast by experts in Africa in a truly South-South network. A low bandwidth is sufficient, and enables the participation from remote hospitals or even cybercafés. Open star parties at dark sites, sidewalk events as well as seminars organised throughout each year further enhance the work to bring astronomy closer to the public through an interactive experience. Commission proposal for the European Competitiveness Fund (ECF), includes for the 2028‑2034 Multi‑annual Financial Framework, a contribution to complementary PNT services, which shall increase the resilience in case of disruptions to the services provided by the PNT component (Article 59). The project shall assess how best can the Commission contribute to complementary PNT services in the next MFF. Leveraging existing national and pan‑European infrastructure, the Commission would like to assess: • How to best strengthen with the resilience of PNT services to radio frequency interference (RFI) affecting GNSS services throughout the EU. • How to best contribute to the deployment of a mature, interoperable C T architecture that is ready for operational use within the multi financial framework 2028 2034. • How to best support candidates for a C-PN service, that utilise the C-T infrastructure and are resilient to RFI and to assess whether the technology is ready for deployment or, if not what is required. Positioning, Navigation and Timing (PNT) functions, delivered principally by Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS) such as the EU owned Galileo, underpin sectors ranging from transport and finance to energy and telecommunications.
